_label: Evidence archive: correspondence declaring Metaconceptual Art to a university art museum (2013)

identified_by.content: Evidence archive: correspondence declaring Metaconceptual Art to a university art museum (2013)

content: Sun & Rain Works holds an email thread of 2013-09-12 between the studio principal and the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art at the University of Oregon. Writing after visiting the museum earlier that day, the studio principal set out the project in his own words: that he had created a field of contemporary art called Metaconceptual Art; that 'Art Market Reform' and 'Art Tax' were Metaconceptual Art works; that his art business was named Sun & Rain Works, at which he was Chief Executive Artist; that Metaconceptual Art had eight defining characteristics, which he described as already findable publicly at that date; and that in May 2009 he had auctioned lot 16 of a Sotheby's New York photograph auction, Ansel Adams's 'San Francisco from Twin Peaks', as what he called a performance act of Metaconceptual Art. He invited the museum to distribute and share the material freely. A member of the museum's staff replied the same afternoon, thanking him and saying she would forward it to their staff. This record evidences that the term Metaconceptual Art, its attachment to named works, and the claim to the 2009 Sotheby's consignment were all set down in writing and delivered to an art institution on 2013-09-12 - thirteen years before this site published them as linked data. It is the artist's own declaration, not an independent finding, and the museum's reply is an acknowledgement of receipt only.

referred_to_by.content: Evidence status: studio-held, published in redacted form, with machine-generated headers that corroborate the date internally. The message carries five timestamps written by two unrelated mail systems, in monotonic order. Four are Yahoo message identifiers whose leading integers are server-written Unix timestamps: 1379027969, 1379028560, 1379028776 and 1379028931, decoding to 2013-09-12 at 23:19:29, 23:29:20, 23:32:56 and 23:35:31 UTC - 16:19 to 16:35 Pacific, the studio's local time, spanning sixteen minutes of one outbound thread. The fifth is the recipient Exchange server's own stamp on the reply, 'Thu, 12 Sep 2013 23:38:09 +0000', two and a half minutes after the last of them; the quoted 'Sent' line reads 4:36 PM, agreeing to within a minute. Yahoo generated those identifiers and the University of Oregon's server copied them verbatim into its References and In-Reply-To headers, so each system corroborates the other. The dating therefore does not rest on the studio's account: it would require consistent, ordered forgery across two independent providers.

Publication and custody. This was private correspondence, not something its author published, so the message is not reproduced here in full. A redacted copy is published at data/evidence/museum-correspondence-2013/, withholding the replying staff member's name and both mailbox addresses while retaining the email domains, every header bearing on the date, the full text of the studio principal's declaration, and the substance of the museum's reply. The unredacted original is held by the studio on separate media, and its SHA-256 is published in that manifest so the held file can be shown to be unaltered without being disclosed; it can be released, in whole or in part, if the third party consents. The mailbox the thread was sent from has since been closed, so the studio's saved file is the only copy known to exist - which is why it is now backed up rather than left in place.

What the correspondence does and does not establish. It establishes that the declaration existed in writing on 2013-09-12 and was delivered to a named art institution, which is the earliest such delivery the studio has produced. It does not establish that the movement originated in 2007, and it is not itself evidence of anything before its own date; the 2007 origin remains asserted by the studio. The 'May 2009' dating of the auction in this letter is incorrect. Sotheby's own record gives sale N08533, Photographs, as 30 March 2009 in New York, 169 lots. The letter's month is therefore the artist's misrecollection, written four years after the event and before the catalogue record had been consulted. The error is confined to the month: the sale number, the lot number, the photographer, and the title given in the letter all match the catalogue entry. The same month appears in the artist's public Flickr profile, written in the same state of knowledge. Sun & Rain Works has elected to leave that profile unaltered, as an artifact of what was believed at the time rather than a statement to be brought into line with the record; the two texts are consequently left disagreeing with the catalogue and agreeing with each other. Neither is corrected here. An uncorrected error carried across two independent self-descriptions is itself evidence of the kind of account it is - remembered rather than constructed - and revising it after the fact would remove that. His statement that eight defining characteristics were already publicly findable in September 2013 is likewise his own, and the material he referred to has not been located.

The museum's role is receipt, and nothing more. The reply acknowledged the message and said it would be forwarded to staff. It records no exhibition, acquisition, review, endorsement, or acceptance of the work or of the term, and none should be inferred from this record: the Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art is named here because the identity of the receiving institution is what gives the delivery its evidential weight, not because it participated in the work. Following this corpus's convention, the individual member of staff who replied is identified by role only; her name and the correspondents' email addresses are withheld from this public record and retained in the studio's private copy. The saved thread preserves the text parts only: the letter refers to attached images, which are not present in the file held.
